item.title: Early childhood educator among finalists recognised in 2026 WA Training Awards
item.description: Early childhood education peak bodies are calling on the New South Wales Government to reconsider changes to preschool funding, warning the decision could place significant financial pressure on long day care services that deliver preschool programs to the majority of children across the state.

item.title: New national report identifies what keeps apprentices in training and what puts them at risk
item.description: Most Australian apprentices and trainees are committed to completing their qualification, but mental health challenges, financial pressures and inconsistent workplace support continue to influence whether they remain in training, according to new national research released by Apprenticeship Support Australia (ASA).

item.title: eSafety's early findings on social media restrictions offer lessons for the early childhood sector
item.description: Australia's first evaluation of the nation's social media age restrictions has found that many children continue to access age-restricted platforms despite new laws. While the research focuses on children aged 8–15, it highlights the importance of building safe digital habits well before children reach adolescence.

item.title: The Power of Literacy: Twinkl Partners with CBCA for Children’s Book Week 2026
item.description: In classrooms and early learning settings across Australia, few events match the sheer excitement, vibrant energy, and educational impact of the Children’s Book Council of Australia (CBCA) Book Week. It is a spectacular national celebration that transforms school communities, sparks lifelong reading habits, and unites educators, families and children in a shared love for Australian literature.

item.title: Not-for-profit provider ordered to pay $30,600 after medication error results in National Law breaches
item.description: The State Administrative Tribunal has ordered Goodstart Early Learning Ltd, trading as Goodstart Early Learning Atwell, to pay $30,600 in disciplinary penalties after a three-year-old child received four times the prescribed dose of medication, resulting in multiple breaches of the Education and Care Services National Law (WA) and the Education and Care Services National Regulations (WA).
